key_insight: CAVQS reduces two-qubit gate costs by jointly exploiting cross-block unitary redistribution and measurement-enabled dynamic circuit reconstruction.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a route to lower CNOT costs, with dynamic-circuit savings requiring permitted terminal measurements and classical feedforward.
method: Use QR decomposition to redistribute unitary factors across overlapping blocks while preserving the overall transformation.
Reshape local synthesis targets to enable simplification across block boundaries.
Build ancilla-free dynamic implementations using CNOT-budgeted pre-measurement search and analytic branch unitaries.
evidence_signal: On common successful random-circuit instances, mean two-qubit gate reductions span 2.05%–74.64% across three baselines; reported reductions on 4–6-qubit algorithm benchmarks span 20.65%–71.88%.
watch_item: Results on small algorithm benchmarks and common successful random instances do not establish larger-scale performance or hardware runtime gains.
paper_title: CAVQS: Context-Aware Variational Quantum Circuit Synthesis via Unitary Redistribution and Dynamic Reconstruction
